messages:
riley: Heads-up: our per-route cost card shows a big prefetch delta vs the settled billing export for acct Y. looks like credits are landing on model SKUs instead of the origin route.
teo: can you share the panel query? my gut says sampling + late join.
riley: panel does `prefetch_ledger SAMPLE (0.05)` then join to `invocations` to attribute. simplified: 
```
select route_id, sum(tokens_saved * token_price) as savings
from prefetch_ledger sample (0.05)
join invocations using (invocation_id)
group by route_id
```
The invoice pipeline uses full-data attribution to model_sku and then backfills route via session mapping.
jordan: that's a problem: sampling BEFORE the join will bias route mapping when invocations are sparse for some routes. We should either sample after joins or emit a route-scoped event at generation time.
nina: product requirement: customers expect to see "what my route saved" in Console. They don't care which internal model got the credit, as long as the route ROI is accurate.
teo: ops concern: if we flip to route-first credits for reporting, we must avoid accidentally changing invoices. proposed path: (a) telemetry-only duplicate events `prefetch_credit_v2` annotated with `origin_route` and `lineage_id`, (b) a feature-flagged Console panel that reads these events, (c) optional billing opt-in for committed tenants.
riley: agree. also need to handle shared cache slabs — credits should be split by measured usage share, and tagged `credit_scope=shared` so we can show both tenant & route slices.
jordan: multi-hop chains add complexity: route triggers model A which triggers model B. If A's prefetch avoided tokens used by B, how do we apportion? suggestions: 1) assign credit to the highest-level route that initiated the chain, 2) or split proportionally across invocations using KV lineage. both require lineage ids.
teo: API design debate: extend /api/costs/rollups with a `?include_prefetch=true` flag vs create /api/costs/prefetch_rollups. I prefer a separate endpoint — different TTLs, heavier joins, and we can return telemetry provenance metadata (sample_rate, estimated_variance).
nina: UX: surface "estimated variance" next to prefetch numbers (small grey text) and a drilldown modal with "how we compute this" and the sampling assumptions. keep default view simple.
riley: infra-bot: note we have a pending deploy of ledger-v2-canary to eng-platform tonight. please ensure telemetry-only events are safe.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: ledger-v2-canary -> eng-platform at 2024-11-06T03:00Z. Canary includes prefactor:emit_route_credit flag.
jordan: tests: unit test the sampling-to-join pipeline to ensure extrapolation factor is applied based on join-time sampling rate, not source sample rate. also add an integration smoke that compares sum(prefetch_ledger_extrapolated) vs prefetch_volume_reported over 24h.
teo: ops also wants `exposure_id` in events to map to canary routing experiments (sticky/dedicated). otherwise we'll see variance and have no signal.
nina: action items: riley -> add lineage + credit_scope (riley). teo -> new endpoint & rate-limits (teo). jordan -> sampling unit-tests + smoke (jordan). nina -> panel mock + tooltip copy. schedule 48h telemetry-only canary then evaluate.
riley: I'll kick off the 48h run and post the comparison. thanks y'all. :rocket:
